citations.narrative:
At least four adult dogs in the kennel were not identified by a tag, tattoo, or microchip. Not having an official identification
on each dog doesn't allow for APHIS officials to be able to properly track the dogs through the kennel. All adult dogs must
be identified by an official tag, tattoo, or microchip. Correct by 9/3/26.

citations.desc: Cleaning, sanitization, housekeeping, and pest control.
citations.narrative:
Feces was accumulating throughout many of the enclosures throughout the kennel. When asked, the licensee stated they
haven't been scooped since at least last Saturday (2 days prior). In addition, I observed an excessive accumulation of
feces underneath the outdoor part of the enclosures. When asked, the licensee stated he has never cleaned under those
enclosures. He stated he has been using this building for approximately five years. The accumulation of feces can
contribute to the spread of disease. Excreta must be removed from the primary enclosures daily and must be removed
from under the primary enclosures as often as necessary to prevent an excessive accumulation of feces.

citations.desc: Cleaning, sanitization, housekeeping, and pest control.
citations.narrative:
At least two doggy doors had grime built up on them. At least two enclosures (one containing a nursing dog and her
puppies) had grime and feces material smeared onto the floor within the enclosure. The licensee wasn't sure exactly
when the enclosures were last sanitized but thought it was pushing two weeks and said it may have been more than two
weeks. At least two enclosures had feeders that had a grimy buildup near the tops of the insides of the feeders. The
licensee stated the feeders haven't been sanitized in the past month and can't actually remember the last time those were
sanitized.
Grime built up on the doggy doors and insides of feeders and fecal material smeared onto the floors of the enclosures can
contribute to the spread of disease. Used primary enclosures and food receptacles must be sanitized every two weeks or
more often as necessary to prevent the accumulation of dirt, debris, excreta, and other disease hazards.

citations.desc: Cleaning, sanitization, housekeeping, and pest control.
citations.narrative:
Pebbles of food were observed throughout the kennel. One corner in the kennel near where food is stored had an
accumulation (pile) of food on the floor. Not sweeping up and keeping the kennel clean and free of food on the ground can
attract rodents and other pests and contribute to the spread of disease. All housing facilities must be kept clean to help
reduce/eliminate rodents and other pests in the kennels which will in turn help reduce the spread of disease.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
End of report.
